brief.headline: The exchange reopens today after four publishing days without a settlement, and it reopens into a month that closed behind it: August 2026 is now final, every average on this page has rolled from July to August, and the completed month says aluminium's mean rose 2.97% to $3,249.63 - its first monthly gain since May, but still only third of five metals, beaten two-to-one by copper and two-and-a-half-to-one by zinc.
bullets: WHAT MOVED TODAY, AND IT IS NOT THE PRICE. The LME was shut on Monday 31-August for the United Kingdom Summer Bank Holiday, so the board is the 28-August official for a fourth publishing day: cash $3,222.00, three-month $3,241.00, a $19.00 contango, stock 246,725 tonnes. What changed is the COMPARISON. Because 31-August was a holiday, 28-August was August's final session, August is a closed month, and from today the prior-month column on every row shows the August mean instead of the July one. Cash therefore flips from $66 above its benchmark to $28 below it without a single trade. That flip is a calendar artefact and is flagged so nobody reads it as a move.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL ROLL. The completed August board ranks aluminium third of five on price and third of five on inventory draw. Copper's monthly mean rose 6.12% and its warehouse average fell 22.6%; zinc rose 7.76% with stock down 14.3%; aluminium rose 2.97% with stock down 11.0%; nickel rose 0.65%; lead rose 0.59% with stock UP 8.9%. Aluminium spent the whole month carrying a Gulf supply premium, a smelter outage at roughly a tenth of world capacity and two producer force majeures. Zinc had no disruption story at all and beat it by a factor of two and a half. That is the closed month's verdict on how much the disruption narrative was actually worth.

THE CURVE SAYS THE SAME THING AND IT SAYS IT MORE BLUNTLY. Across August aluminium's cash mean of $3,249.63 sat BELOW its three-month mean of $3,251.23 - a $1.60 average CONTANGO over twenty sessions, a market declining for a full month to pay anything for prompt metal. Copper averaged a $197.67 BACKWARDATION over the same days. Note the opposite-direction combination on aluminium specifically: the flat price ROSE while the curve LOOSENED out of July's small backwardation into August's contango. Price up, structure softer, is the signature of a market lifted by macro and currency rather than by scarcity at the front.

WHAT TO WATCH IN THE NEXT TWELVE HOURS. Today's 13:20 London official is the first in four days and carries two unpriced items. Currency: the board still shown here was struck against an EUR/USD fixing of 1.16460, while the 31-August ECB fixing was 1.15960 - a 0.43% stronger dollar that no LME figure has yet absorbed, so if all six metals open lower together that is the currency. Geopolitics: the Strait of Hormuz re-escalated over the weekend, with US strikes on Larak Island on 30-August and an IRGC claim that a supertanker struck mines, and Brent rose 3.19% to $90.91 while London was closed. Then US ISM manufacturing at 14:00 GMT, consensus 55.2, into a market that has repriced toward Fed hikes with the 10-year at 4.725%.

drivers.text: Section 232 verified at 50% on articles, 25% on derivatives - and the carve-out structure matters — Re-verified against the primary source this run rather than carried. Proclamation 11032 of 01-June-2026, published at 91 FR 34085 on 04-June-2026 and effective 08-June-2026, leaves the Annex I-A rate on aluminium articles at 50% and the Annex I-B derivative rate at 25%, with a 15% temporary subset for fixed industrial machinery and power equipment now extended to agricultural equipment and residential HVAC. THE ANNEX I-C CARVE-OUT LIST IS THE PART MOST OFTEN MISREAD: for Argentina, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Japan, Korea, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, Taiwan, the United Kingdom and any EU member state, the effective rate is set by the product's HTSUS Column 1 duty - 15% total where Column 1 is below 15%, and no Section 232 addition where Column 1 is at or above 15%. Canada and Mexico under USMCA pay 25% on non-US content only, with a 15% floor. The US-origin content threshold was lowered from 95% to 85% by weight.
drivers.source: Federal Register - Proclamation 11032, 91 FR 34085, further adjusting the tariff regimes for aluminum, steel and copper, effective 08-Jun-2026

drivers.text: The US-Canada framework is reported, not law - and it already moved the premium 8.2% in one session — A tentative framework that would cut US tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminium from 50% to 25% was reported on 19-August-2026. drivers.text: The Q4-2026 Japanese round opens now, into a spot market trading below the record Q3 settlement — Q3-2026 settled at $395/t CIF Japan on 06-July-2026, a record, up 12.4% on Q2's $351.50/t. US forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers on LARAK ISLAND, adjacent to the Strait, on SUNDAY 30-AUGUST; Iran retaliated against US bases; and the IRGC has claimed that a supertanker caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait. THE COUNTER-SIGNAL IS EQUALLY DATED AND IS GIVEN EQUAL WEIGHT RATHER THAN BURIED: on 01-SEPTEMBER President Trump stated that strikes against Iran would be LIMITED and that the Strait of Hormuz is 'in very good condition' with large volumes of oil moving out, while Treasury Secretary Bessent confirmed expanded secondary sanctions on Iran's trading partners and attributed the Iranian military action to sanctions pressure. THE TWO READS ARE NOT RECONCILED HERE BECAUSE THE MARKET HAS NOT RECONCILED THEM EITHER - Brent rose 3.19% to $90.91 on the escalation while the LME was closed and could not respond at all. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR ALUMINIUM SPECIFICALLY: roughly 9% of global primary supply exits via this waterway and more than 80% of Gulf production is exported through it. The re-escalation lands on a market that had just begun to price the corridor as a supply-relief event, and today's 13:20 London official is the first opportunity for the exchange to express a view on any of it. THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ RE-ESCALATED OVER THE WEEKEND AND REVERSED THE DE-ESCALATION THIS PAGE HAD CARRIED SINCE 26-AUGUST. US forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers on LARAK ISLAND, adjacent to the Strait, on SUNDAY 30-AUGUST; Iran retaliated against US bases; the IRGC claims a supertanker caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait. Reporting on 31-August describes the renewed hostilities as having dashed hopes of near-term normalisation of transit. THE COUNTER-SIGNAL IS EQUALLY DATED: on 01-September President Trump stated that strikes would be LIMITED and that the Strait is 'in very good condition' with large oil volumes moving out, while Treasury Secretary Bessent confirmed expanded secondary sanctions on Iran's trading partners. The US 10-year sits at 4.725% having closed near 4.75%, the highest since early 2026; the 30-year is at a two-decade high; the 10-year JGB is the highest since 1996; the German 10-year is at 3.307%. Higher real discount rates raise the cost of carrying inventory, tighten the financing of physical positions and compress the demand outlook that every deficit thesis on this page depends on.

A USEFUL COUNTERWEIGHT TO THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM PICTURE RATHER THAN A CONTRADICTION OF IT, AND THE DISTINCTION IS GEOGRAPHIC. earnings.note: H1-2026 interim results: alumina sales volume 1.296 Mt (+15.0% y/y from ~1.127 Mt) but average realised selling price USD 320/t against USD 529/t (-39.5%); revenue USD 415.0m (-30.5% y/y from USD 596.8m); gross profit USD 65.5m from USD 303.9m; gross margin 15.8% from 50.9%; profit attributable USD 62.7m (-74.8%); basic EPS USD 0.10 from USD 0.46; interim dividend cut to HKD 0.16 from HKD 0.65. Cash and equivalents more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings; total assets USD 2.496bn (+11.0%). THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. Hydro cut the 6.3 Mtpa refinery to 50% on 11-AUGUST-2026 after gas supplier CELBA notified disruptions, and then announced on 13-AUGUST-2026 that it was RAMPING BACK UP, after Brazil's ANP approved Alunorte as a gas self-importer and a temporary terminal-access arrangement was struck with CELBA. The practical consequence is that the largest alumina refinery outside China is not a live supply constraint today, which removes one leg from the bull case this page carried through August.

Alba initiated a controlled and safe shutdown of reduction Lines 1, 2 and 3 in mid-March 2026 to preserve business continuity amid the Strait of Hormuz disruption, idling 19% of its 1,623,000 tpa capacity; asset care and maintenance are being carried out on the idled lines to enable a safe restart 'when conditions permit'. Alba has signalled an intention to REPLACE Lines 1-3 with newer, more efficient facilities rather than simply restart them, which would make the loss structural rather than temporary. FINANCIALLY THE CURTAILMENT HAS NOT HURT: H1-2026 attributable profit was BHD 140.2m (about $372.8m), up 228% year on year, with Q2-2026 at BHD 64.9m despite Q2 output falling 61%. THE LIMIT OF WHAT IS KNOWN IS STATED: no public announcement of a Lines 1-3 restart could be found, so '3 of 6 lines down' is the last publicly confirmed state as of the March disclosure rather than a 01-September confirmation.

status.name: Century Aluminum (CENX)
status.status: MT HOLLY AT FULL CAPACITY FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE 2015; 2026 GUIDANCE HELD
status.impact: Bearish (US supply added and confirmed complete)
status.update: Century has restarted the final 90 pots at Mt Holly, taking the smelter to FULL CAPACITY FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE 2015 - on time and on budget, roughly $50m of spend, about 150 full-time positions added, more than 50,000 t of idled capacity returned, and a lift of nearly 10% to total US primary aluminium production. The restart began on 16-April. Q2-2026, reported 06-August: net sales $752.1m, net income attributable $249.3m, adjusted diluted EPS $2.46, adjusted EBITDA attributable $326.9m, shipments 130,632 t up 6% quarter on quarter. Q3-2026 guidance assumes a lagged LME of $3,330/t, $75 above the Q2 realised price, and guides a $15-25m adjusted EBITDA benefit from the first full quarter of expanded Mt Holly.

status.name: Alcoa (AA)
status.status: SAN CIPRIAN RESTART COMPLETE; PORTLAND POWER SECURED TO MID-2035; SOUTH32 ACQUISITION SIGNED, CLOSE GUIDED H1-2027
status.update: The San Ciprian smelter restart COMPLETED ON 07-APRIL-2026 and was the primary reason Alcoa's Q2-2026 aluminium production rose 5% quarter on quarter to 636 kt. Portland in Victoria is operating with power secured to mid-2035 through a 300 MW AGL contract plus a nine-year 287 MW contract that took effect 01-JULY-2026; combined, those support up to 95% of the 358 ktpa nameplate against a recent running rate near 80%. NO 2026-DATED PORTLAND OPERATIONAL UPDATE WAS FOUND, so that status rests on the contract announcement rather than a current confirmation, and it is flagged as such. THE SOUTH32 TRANSACTION IS THE LARGER STRUCTURAL ITEM: announced 30-June-2026 at $4.1bn ($3.1bn cash plus about 17.0m Alcoa shares), an implied enterprise value near $4.7bn including assumed lease debt, plus a contingent value right worth up to $750m tied to alumina and aluminium price strikes. It adds roughly 18 Mt of attributable bauxite and 5 Mt of attributable alumina annually and raises Alcoa's smelting capacity by about 26%. IT HAS NOT CLOSED - completion is guided to H1-2027 subject to South32 shareholder approval and regulatory clearances.
src: Alcoa - strategic acquisition of South32's bauxite, alumina and aluminium assets for $4.1bn, 30-Jun-2026

status.name: Rio Tinto (RIO) / Tomago
status.status: SECURED - GOVERNMENT SUPPORT PACKAGE AND A 10-YEAR PPA TO 2038
status.impact: Bearish (a smelter that might have closed will not)
status.update: Australia's largest aluminium smelter has been underwritten. Federal and New South Wales governments are providing support reported at approximately A$2.5bn through 2038, split roughly evenly, against Tomago commitments of at least A$1.1bn in capital works and maintenance plus A$100m on decarbonisation, preserving around 1,000 jobs. A 10-YEAR POWER PURCHASE AGREEMENT RUNS TO 2038, starting after the current contract expires on 31-December-2028, with 100% renewable supply from 2033. THE HEADLINE DOLLAR FIGURE IS INCONSISTENT ACROSS PUBLIC SOURCES - A$2.5bn combined versus A$1.76bn or US$1.8bn in other reporting, apparently a scope difference - and Rio Tinto's own release is treated as primary here. The market significance is simple: capacity that the market had a reasonable case for retiring is now committed for another decade.

status.name: Slovalco (Hydro) / Magnitude 7 Metals
status.status: RESTARTS CONFIRMED - 75 kt EACH, BOTH LANDING BY OR IN Q4-2026
status.update: Both restarts remain on their published timetable and neither is speculative. Hydro's Slovalco resumes 75 kt from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals restarts the No. 1 potline at Marston, Missouri for 75 kt/y by end-2026. Together with Century's completed Mt Holly expansion, Alcoa's completed San Ciprian and Portland restarts and EGA's Al Taweelah ramp, these constitute a Western supply-restoration pipeline that is dated, published and already partly delivered. THE MARKET IMPLICATION IS THE ONE THIS PAGE HAS MADE ALL MONTH AND THE COMPLETED AUGUST BOARD SUPPORTS IT: the disruption premium is being unwound on a schedule the market can read, which is why aluminium's monthly average gain of 2.97% finished third of five behind metals with no disruption story at all.

status.name: China operators (aggregate, incl. Chalco and Hongqiao)
status.status: AT OR THROUGH THE 45 Mt POLICY CEILING; OUTPUT STABLE, MARGINS WIDE, EXPORTS ELEVATED

THE MARGIN PICTURE IS THE MORE IMPORTANT SUPPLY FACT AND IT IS PUBLISHED: SMM reports China's weighted all-in production cost DOWN 0.7% month on month and 3.4% year on year in August, a smelter margin averaging RMB 7,890/t over the 26-July to 25-August window - up 87.7% year on year - and 100% OF OPERATING CAPACITY PROFITABLE. Chalco released its 2026 interim results on 27-August; the headline figures were not independently verified against the company filing this run and are therefore not restated here.

status.name: US / Canada trade policy (Section 232)
status.status: 50% ON ARTICLES, 25% ON DERIVATIVES - VERIFIED; A US-CANADA CUT TO 25% IS REPORTED BUT NOT LAW
status.impact: Mixed (the largest single swing factor in the US delivered premium)
status.update: Verified against the primary source this run. Proclamation 11032 of 01-June-2026, published at 91 FR 34085 and effective 08-June-2026, holds the Annex I-A rate on aluminium articles at 50% and the Annex I-B derivative rate at 25%, with a 15% temporary subset now extended to agricultural equipment and residential HVAC, and aluminium lithographic plates newly brought into coverage. Annex I-C sets a 15% effective ceiling for a listed group including Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and EU member states, 10% where derivative aluminium content is entirely US-smelted and cast, and 25% on non-US content only for USMCA-qualifying Canadian and Mexican goods with a 15% floor. THE PENDING CHANGE IS REPORTED, NOT ENACTED: a tentative framework to halve the Canadian rate to 25% was reported 19-August and drove an 8.2% single-session collapse in the September Midwest premium to 95.0 c/lb on 20-August. Commerce has separately offered a cut to 25% for producers that build or expand US facilities.

trade.note: TRADE CORRIDORS ARE REVIEWED MONTHLY OR ON MATERIAL CHANGE RATHER THAN REFRESHED DAILY. THEY ARE RE-RATED THIS RUN, AND THE TRIGGER IS SPECIFIC RATHER THAN A CALENDAR DATE: the Strait of Hormuz de-escalation that this page carried from 26-August - an Iran-Oman announcement of a planned safe maritime corridor - BROKE DOWN OVER THE WEEKEND. US forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island, adjacent to the Strait, on Sunday 30-AUGUST; Iran retaliated against US bases; and the IRGC has claimed that a supertanker caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait. Reporting on 31-August describes the renewed hostilities as having dashed hopes of near-term normalisation of transit, and Brent rose 3.19% to $90.91 on it while the LME was closed. THE COUNTER-SIGNAL IS GIVEN EQUAL WEIGHT AND IS EQUALLY DATED: on 01-September President Trump stated that strikes against Iran would be LIMITED and that the Strait is 'in very good condition' with large volumes of oil moving out, while Treasury Secretary Bessent confirmed expanded secondary sanctions on Iran's trading partners and attributed the Iranian action to sanctions pressure. THE TWO READS ARE NOT RECONCILED HERE BECAUSE THE MARKET HAS NOT RECONCILED THEM EITHER, and no LME session has yet had the opportunity to express a view. SECOND STRUCTURAL POINT, UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE BUT NOW SIMULTANEOUS WITH THE FIRST: Bab el Mandeb transits are down roughly 24% since the Houthi maritime blockade imposed on Saudi Arabia in July 2026, and US MARAD advisory 2026-006 remains in force through 22-SEPTEMBER-2026. Both Middle East chokepoints are impaired at the same time, which leaves a Gulf or Red Sea shipper with no unimpaired routing to Europe and is the physical reason freight is inflating faster than any other cost on this page. THIRD, THE SANCTIONS CLOCK: the LME has required attestations to warrant Russian aluminium in EU-listed warehouses since 25-February-2026, and the EU import ban on Russian aluminium takes effect 31-DECEMBER-2026 - a dated, certain change to the availability of the metal that dominates LME warrantable stock.

flows.impact: Rising - and it is now the principal mechanism relieving the Western shortage
flows.note: Semi-finished exports 3.2 Mt in January-June, +18% year on year, with June at a record 695,000 t. Alloy exports nearly doubled to 238,500 t and China turned NET EXPORTER of aluminium alloy in June for the first time since 2019. Primary exports +32% to 38,400 t, much of it likely Western-origin bonded metal being redirected rather than Chinese production leaving. Driven by a tax structure that charges 30% on primary exports and zero on alloy and semis, and enabled by soft domestic demand - Citi's China end-use tracker fell 0.4% year on year while primary production rose 2.2%. The corridor consequence is that the Western physical shortage is being relieved WITHOUT unwrought metal changing hands, which is one public explanation for how a primary deficit can coexist with a flat or discounted LME front end.
src: AL Circle - China eases aluminium shortage after Iran war, but pressure shifts to Western fabricators, 18-Aug-2026

flows.note: RE-RATED THIS RUN ON MATERIAL CHANGE. About 9% of global primary supply exits via the Strait of Hormuz and more than 80% of Gulf production is exported through it. THE CORRIDOR RE-ESCALATED OVER THE WEEKEND after a week in which this page had carried a de-escalation: US strikes on two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on 30-August, Iranian retaliation against US bases, and an IRGC claim that a supertanker caught fire after striking naval mines. Brent rose 3.19% to $90.91 on it. President Trump stated on 01-September that strikes would be limited and the Strait is 'in very good condition' with large oil volumes moving; both statements are dated and both are carried. THE PHYSICAL POSITION BEHIND THE HEADLINES IS THE PART THAT HAS NOT CHANGED: Qatalum remains at roughly 60% of its 648 kt nameplate on reduced gas with no published restart timetable and a second Hydro force majeure outstanding; Alba has reduction Lines 1, 2 and 3 idled since March, 19% of 1,623 kt, with no announced restart and a stated intention to replace rather than restart them; EGA's Al Taweelah smelter is at 25% of cells with full production reaffirmed for Q1-2027. Gulf primary output ran roughly 40% below pre-war levels in April. This is the one corridor on the page where the disruption is both real and, in Qatalum's and Alba's cases, undated.
src: Bloomberg / Kpler via public reporting - Iran-Oman Hormuz route agreement and transit counts (05-Aug-2026)

flows.note: THE RED SEA IS DIVERGING FROM HORMUZ. Bab al Mandeb traffic fell to a weekly low of 16 commodity vessels on 26-Jul after the Houthi 'embargo' on Saudi shipping declared 20-Jul and claimed attacks on Aramco sites at Jizan and Yanbu, recovering only to 31 by 31-Jul. On 05-Aug Houthi forces claimed they had targeted a Saudi oil tanker in the Gulf of Aden and threatened further vessels in the Red Sea, with a ship reported hit the same day. A Hormuz routing agreement does not address this constraint. Saudi Arabia has been diverting crude to the Suez routing; the Suez leg for Gulf and Red Sea origin cargoes is therefore still not a clean alternative to Hormuz.

~60% of global primary output; the 45 Mt capacity cap is binding at 45.31 Mt/y operating. The July twist is compositional: the liquid-aluminium proportion rose to 78.3% with casting-ingot volume -15.1% y/y, so less deliverable ingot reaches the domestic market even at capped output - semis exports remain the swing valve between the domestic balance and the ex-China deficit.

catalysts.text: THE FIRST LME OFFICIAL IN FOUR PUBLISHING DAYS, AND IT CARRIES TWO SPECIFIC, MEASURABLE, UNPRICED TESTS. Monday 31-August was the UK Summer Bank Holiday and the exchange was shut, following the weekend; 28-August has now been republished four times. FIRST, CURRENCY: the 28-August board was settled against an EUR/USD LME fixing of 1.16460, while the 31-August ECB fixing - verified on both the English and cache-busted German Westmetall overviews - was 1.15960. That is a 0.43% stronger dollar that no LME figure on this page has absorbed. If ALL SIX METALS open lower together, that is the currency and not aluminium. SECOND, GEOPOLITICS: Brent rose 3.19% to $90.91 on the weekend Hormuz re-escalation while London was closed. If aluminium alone outperforms the board, the Gulf risk premium is being re-paid after a month in which the completed averages showed it had stopped being paid.

US ISM MANUFACTURING FOR AUGUST - CONSENSUS 55.2 AGAINST A PRIOR 55.6. The highest-weight single release before Friday's payrolls, landing into a market that has just repriced toward Fed HIKES rather than cuts after Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole debut. THE ASYMMETRY IS UNCOMFORTABLE FOR AN INDUSTRIAL METAL AND IS WORTH STATING PLAINLY: a strong print reinforces the hawkish read that has the 10-year at 4.725% and the 30-year at a two-decade high, which is bearish through the discount rate; a weak print is bearish through demand. Good news on activity is now also news about the cost of money. Euro-area flash CPI and unemployment, US JOLTS and a Fed Governor Barr speech at 13:05 GMT complete the day.

US NON-FARM PAYROLLS - THE WEEK'S DOMINANT EVENT. With a new Fed Chair who was hawkish in his Jackson Hole debut, a market pricing hike risk, the US 30-year at a two-decade high, the 10-year JGB the highest since 1996 and the German 10-year at 3.307%, payrolls is the release that either validates or breaks the repricing that has driven global yields to cycle highs. Base metals have no defence against a hawkish surprise and only a weaker-dollar consolation from a dovish one.

THE CHINESE DESTOCK TEST AND THE PMI DISAGREEMENT. Aluminium ingot social inventory reached 837,000 t on Monday 31-August, down 15,000 t on the prior Thursday, with a cumulative August destock of 106,000 t and 278,000 t off the early-July peak; SMM expects the draw to continue through the first half of September. A destock that continues counter-seasonally into September would be the strongest physical argument available against a completed month that ranked aluminium third of five. Set against it, the official NBS manufacturing PMI at 49.8 and the private RatingDog index at 51.5 disagree about August, and China's aluminium PROCESSING composite PMI at 48.7% is unambiguously still contracting.

THE JAPANESE Q4-2026 PREMIUM ROUND CONVENTIONALLY OPENS NOW AND HAS NOT OPENED PUBLICLY. Q3-2026 settled at a record $395/t CIF Japan on 06-July, up 12.4% on Q2's $351.50/t, against producer opening offers of $480/t from South32 and $460/t from Rio Tinto. THE PUBLIC SPOT BACKDROP IS UNHELPFUL FOR SELLERS AND IS THE BEST AVAILABLE GUIDE TO WHERE Q4 LANDS: MJP spot peaked in Q2, inflected down from July and kept falling through August, trading notably below the $395 benchmark with sellers struggling to transact and buyers holding out. A spot market below the prevailing settlement going into the quarter that settlement covers is the standard set-up for a lower round. The Q4-2026 cell on this page carries a scenario range and a null value rather than a forecast.

GUINEA BAUXITE EXPORT RESTRICTIONS - TIMING AND FORM STILL UNCONFIRMED, AND THE PRE-BUILD IS ALREADY VISIBLE IN THE FLOW DATA. Global bauxite seaborne flows reached 20 Mt in July 2026, up 3% year on year, as shipments to China surged specifically ahead of the expected curbs; AL Circle cautions in the same report that July strength may not carry forward for exactly that reason. Guinea's approach is understood to be site-specific export limits tied to feasibility-study volumes rather than an Indonesia-style outright ban. A stock-build ahead of an undefined restriction pulls demand forward and leaves an air pocket behind it, and imported bauxite CIF is the driver SMM names behind rising Chinese alumina production costs.

THE MONTHLY CARBON SETTLEMENT CYCLE - THE NEXT CHANCE FOR THE COAL-TAR-PITCH SERIES ON THIS PAGE TO GAIN A REAL POINT. Prebaked anode and coal-tar-pitch settlements conventionally print around the 17th-18th. The September anode tender has already printed at RMB 5,730/t, up RMB 100 month on month, and PetroChina raised North-East China low-sulphur petcoke list prices effective 01-September, so the direction into the pitch settlement is up. The pitch series on this page ends at RMB 4,960/t on 13-August and the gap has been left as a gap rather than interpolated, because SMM's fortnightly anode reviews that carried the free number are now behind a subscription wall.

TWO DATED, CERTAIN SUPPLY-SIDE CHANGES LAND IN THE SAME QUARTER AND THEY PULL IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. FIRST, WESTERN CAPACITY RETURNS: Hydro's Slovalco resumes 75 kt from Q4-2026 and Magnitude 7 Metals restarts the No. 1 potline at Marston, Missouri for 75 kt/y by end-2026, on top of a Mt Holly expansion already complete and a San Ciprian restart already complete. SECOND, AVAILABLE METAL IS REMOVED: the EU import ban on Russian aluminium takes effect on 31-DECEMBER-2026, against Russian-origin metal that has dominated warrantable LME stock through 2026, with LME attestations already required to warrant it in EU-listed warehouses since 25-February. A market whose visible inventory has already stopped falling faces a supply addition and a warrant-eligibility contraction in the same three months.

risks.text: SUPPLY RELIEF ARRIVES ON A DATED, PUBLISHED SCHEDULE AND CAPS THE RECOVERY - STILL THE DOMINANT RISK ON THIS BOARD, AND THE CLOSED AUGUST MONTH IS NOW THE EVIDENCE RATHER THAN THE ARGUMENT. The timetable is public and it advanced again this week: EGA's Al Taweelah smelter is at 25% of cells - 315 of 1,262, up from roughly 18% a week ago - with all three potlines being worked and full production reaffirmed for Q1-2027; Century's Mt Holly is at FULL capacity for the first time since 2015, adding nearly 10% to total US primary output; Alcoa's San Ciprian restart completed in April and Portland has power secured to mid-2035; Hydro's Slovalco resumes 75 kt from Q4-2026 and Magnitude 7 Metals restarts 75 kt at Marston by end-2026; Tomago is underwritten to 2038 by a government package and a 10-year PPA. A CORRECTION MADE OPENLY THIS RUN REINFORCES THE POINT: this page had carried Alunorte at roughly 50% of capacity, but Hydro announced on 13-August that it was ramping the 6.3 Mtpa refinery back to FULL after ANP approved it as a gas self-importer. The largest alumina refinery outside China is not a live constraint. THE PRICE ALREADY KNOWS: aluminium's completed August monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, and its curve averaged a $1.60 contango against copper's $197.67 backwardation.

THE STOCK DRAW HAS STOPPED, AND THE COMPLETED MONTH NOW SHOWS EXACTLY WHEN IT STOPPED. LME aluminium warehouse stock fell from 262,650 t on 03-August to 246,925 t on 17-August and then moved 200 TONNES ACROSS THE FINAL NINE SESSIONS OF THE MONTH, closing at 246,725 t. The draw did not decelerate gradually - it halted, and it halted three weeks before the month ended. August's average stock of 251,215 t against July's 282,350 t is an 11.0% monthly decline, which is real but ranks THIRD of five: copper -22.6%, zinc -14.3%, aluminium -11.0%, nickel -2.2%, lead +8.9%. A DEFICIT NARRATIVE REQUIRES INVENTORY TO KEEP FALLING; this one has flatlined at a level that is historically low but no longer directional, while the metal sitting on it is disproportionately Russian-origin ahead of a 31-December-2026 EU import ban. THE ONE GENUINE COUNTERWEIGHT IS CHINESE AND IT IS CONSTRUCTIVE: ingot social inventory fell to 837,000 t on 31-August, down 15,000 t on the prior Thursday and 23,000 t on the prior Monday, for a cumulative August destock of 106,000 t and 278,000 t off the early-July peak - counter-seasonal, and SMM expects it to continue through the first half of September.

GULF SUPPLY DISRUPTION IS REAL AND PARTLY UNDATED, BUT THE MARKET HAS STOPPED PAYING FOR IT - AND THE WEEKEND RE-ESCALATION IS THE TEST OF WHETHER THAT HOLDS. THE TREND IS RAISED TO UP THIS RUN AND THE REASON IS A DATED EVENT RATHER THAN A CHANGE OF MOOD: the Iran-Oman safe maritime corridor that this page carried from 26-August broke down when US forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on 30-AUGUST, Iran retaliated against US bases, and the IRGC claimed a supertanker caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait. Brent rose 3.19% to $90.91 on it while the LME was closed and could not respond. THE COUNTER-SIGNAL IS EQUALLY DATED: on 01-September President Trump stated strikes would be LIMITED and the Strait is 'in very good condition' with large oil volumes moving. THE PHYSICAL POSITION IS THE PART THAT HAS NOT MOVED IN MONTHS: Qatalum at roughly 60% of 648 kt on reduced gas with NO published restart timetable and a second Hydro force majeure outstanding; Alba's reduction Lines 1-3 idled since March, 19% of 1,623 kt, with no announced restart and a stated intention to REPLACE rather than restart them; Gulf primary output running roughly 40% below pre-war levels in April. Two of those three losses have no end date at all, which is more than can be said for any other supply item on this page.

PHYSICAL DEMAND FAILS TO SHOW UP FOR THE PEAK SEASON, AND CHINA'S OWN SURVEYS NOW DISAGREE ABOUT WHETHER IT IS COMING. TREND HELD AT DOWN, BECAUSE THE HARD INVENTORY DATA IS THE ONE SERIES POINTING THE RIGHT WAY. The official NBS manufacturing PMI printed 49.8 for August, up from 49.2 but in contraction for a second month, with employment at 48.7 and non-manufacturing at 49.0; the private RatingDog index printed 51.5 against 50.9 expected, a substantial beat. The official panel skews to large state heavy industry and the private one to smaller exporters, and they have diverged repeatedly through 2026, so the August China demand signal is UNRESOLVED rather than positive. China's aluminium PROCESSING composite PMI is unambiguous, though, at 48.7% - up slightly but still contracting, with September expected to return to expansion. PV frame operating rates are strong on POLICY-DRIVEN advance stockpiling ahead of an expected US Section 232 solar rule rather than on end demand, with forward oversupply pressure behind it. Against all of that, ingot social inventory keeps falling counter-seasonally and European foil deliveries rose 5.8% quarter on quarter in Q2. The physical draw is the better evidence and it is why this trend stays down.

MACRO AND RATES OVERWHELM THE MICRO - RAISED THIS RUN, AND THIS IS THE RISK THAT CHANGED MOST OVER THE WEEKEND. New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh was hawkish in his Jackson Hole debut on Friday 28-August; the selloff carried through Monday; MARKETS ARE NOW PRICING RATE-HIKE RISK RATHER THAN CUTS, and ECB officials are leaning toward a September hike. The US 10-year sits at 4.725% having closed near 4.75%, the highest since early 2026; the 30-year is at a two-decade high; the 10-year JGB is the highest since 1996; the German 10-year is at 3.307%. EVERY TRANSMISSION CHANNEL RUNS THE WRONG WAY FOR AN INDUSTRIAL METAL: higher real rates raise the cost of financing physical inventory, which is the mechanism that turns a contango into forced selling rather than into storage; they compress the demand outlook that every deficit forecast on this page depends on; and a firmer dollar mechanically lowers a dollar-denominated price. The specific unpriced item into today's reopen is measurable: the board carried here was struck against an EUR/USD fixing of 1.16460 and the 31-August ECB fixing was 1.15960, a 0.43% stronger dollar that no LME figure has absorbed.

INPUT-COST INFLATION THROUGH FREIGHT, CARBON AND BAUXITE - HELD AT UP, WITH TWO NEW DATED POINTS THIS RUN. The carbon chain turned: a large Shandong smelter set its SEPTEMBER prebaked anode tender at RMB 5,730/t, UP RMB 100 month on month, ending four months of drift; and PetroChina raised low-sulphur petroleum coke list prices at ALL FIVE of its North-East China refineries effective 00:00 on 01-September. SMM's cost note adds that fluoride salts rose through August with further increases expected in September, and that coal gains will push September power tariffs moderately higher. Freight is the largest single inflation: the Baltic Dry Index closed at 3,186 on 28-August, its seventh consecutive gain and highest since 02-June, up 21.05% on the month and 57.33% on the year, Capesize-led - which is the ore-and-bauxite end. Imported bauxite CIF is the driver SMM names behind rising Chinese alumina costs. THE HONEST COUNTERWEIGHT, AND IT IS LARGE: SMM puts China's weighted all-in production cost DOWN 0.7% month on month and 3.4% year on year in August, with an average smelter margin of RMB 7,890/t - up 87.7% year on year - and 100% of operating capacity profitable. A RMB 100/t anode increase against a RMB 7,890/t margin is a rounding item, which is precisely why cost inflation is a margin risk and not a supply-side price support.

ALUMINA LOOSENS FASTER THAN METAL AND THE SMELTER MARGIN STOPS BEING A CONSTRAINT ON ANYONE'S OUTPUT - TREND SET TO DOWN THIS RUN, MEANING THE RISK OF AN ALUMINA-DRIVEN COST SQUEEZE IS FALLING RATHER THAN THE RISK ITSELF BEING BENIGN. The SMM Alumina Index averaged RMB 2,695/t across the 26-July to 25-August window, DOWN 1.8% month on month; 30,000 t traded at $379/mt FOB Indonesia on 31-August for October shipment; Hydro's Alunorte is ramping back to full after its August gas interruption rather than sitting at 50%; EGA's Al Taweelah refinery is at roughly 50% and rising. THE CONSEQUENCE IS BEARISH FOR METAL EVEN THOUGH IT IS BULLISH FOR SMELTERS, and the distinction is the point: with 100% of Chinese operating capacity profitable and margins up 87.7% year on year, there is no cost-side mechanism anywhere in the world forcing a curtailment. Every tonne that can run, runs. China's domestic alumina at RMB 2,600-2,700 against a national weighted full cost of RMB 2,718/t is the one floor in the system, and it is a floor under alumina, not under aluminium.

US TRADE POLICY MOVES THE DELIVERED PREMIUM MORE THAN THE PHYSICAL MARKET DOES, AND THE PRICED-IN RELIEF HAS NOT BEEN ENACTED. HELD AT UP. Section 232 is verified at 50% on aluminium articles and 25% on derivatives under Proclamation 11032 of 01-June-2026, 91 FR 34085. At the 28-August cash official of $3,222.00 that is $1,611/t of pure duty, which is roughly 77% of a US Midwest duty-paid premium of $2,094/t - the American premium is predominantly a policy variable, not a tightness variable. THE EVIDENCE IS A SINGLE SESSION: an unconfirmed report on 19-August that the US would halve the Canadian rate to 25% took the September Midwest transaction premium DOWN 8.2% to 95.0 c/lb the next day, with October and November down more than 12%, while nothing physical changed. The framework is still not law and not across the board. THE EUROPEAN READ-ACROSS IS THE SECOND-ORDER RISK AND IT IS PUBLICLY FLAGGED: Canadian metal redirected to Europe during the 50% regime flows back to the US if the rate halves, tightening America and loosening Rotterdam simultaneously.

BOTH MIDDLE EAST CHOKEPOINTS ARE IMPAIRED SIMULTANEOUSLY AND DELIVERED COST HAS NO UNIMPAIRED ROUTING - RAISED TO UP THIS RUN. Hormuz re-escalated on 30-August with US strikes on Larak Island and an IRGC claim that a supertanker struck naval mines; Bab el Mandeb transits are down roughly 24% since the July Houthi blockade on Saudi Arabia, with US MARAD advisory 2026-006 in force through 22-September; Suez traffic remains far below pre-crisis normal with carriers still routing via the Cape and adding 10-14 days to Asia-Europe voyages. NO WAR-RISK REPRICING HAS BEEN PUBLISHED SINCE THE WEEKEND STRIKES, so the 7.5-10%-of-hull value mark from 22-July - against a 1-3% pre-conflict norm - should be treated as a floor rather than a current quote. This is a delivered-cost risk that sits inside every regional premium on this page at once and is invisible in the LME flat price.

CARBON BORDER POLICY AND CERTIFICATION BECOME CONDITIONS OF MARKET ACCESS RATHER THAN DIFFERENTIATORS - HELD AT UP, WITH A DATED PROCEDURAL WARNING ADDED THIS RUN. ALFED, the UK Aluminium Federation, briefed the UK government on 28-AUGUST-2026 that key UK CBAM questions remain unresolved ahead of the JANUARY 2027 start - default emissions values, verification and accreditation arrangements, and recognition of overseas carbon costs. EU CBAM costs have already been embedded in the Fastmarkets Rotterdam billet assessment since 01-January-2026. The LME has required attestations to warrant Russian aluminium in EU-listed warehouses since 25-February-2026 and the EU import ban takes effect 31-DECEMBER-2026, against Russian-origin metal dominating available LME stock. THE COMMERCIAL POINT IS THAT UNRESOLVED RULES FOUR MONTHS BEFORE A START DATE ARE THEMSELVES A COST: they force optionality into contracts, widen bid-offer on anything crossing a carbon border, and fall hardest on producers whose verification chain is not already built.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED BUT THE 19-AUGUST DATA SHARPENS HOW A DEFICIT CAN COEXIST WITH A LOOSENING FRONT END. Refined production outside China has fallen year on year for a second consecutive quarter and output outside China fell 6.7% year on year in July, so the annual deficit is real. Yet LME warrant has now been exactly unchanged on two consecutive sessions and the cash-3M spread has printed a widening contango on both. A deficit is an annual flow concept; a contango is a statement about prompt availability at a specific delivery point. THE RECONCILIATION MOST CONSISTENT WITH THE EVIDENCE, AND IT IS A HYPOTHESIS RATHER THAN A FACT, is that visible ex-China exchange stock is reported to be overwhelmingly Russian-origin material Western buyers cannot use - in which case the exchange series measures something different from accessible Western metal, and a global deficit can coexist with an LME front end that will not pay for prompt delivery. Supporting that reading, the Chinese physical market tightened on 20-August even as the LME curve loosened, with holders withholding and spot quotations firming to a small premium, and SHFE warrants continue to draw at roughly double the LME's monthly rate.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.
